subject.title: Durable core PR2/6: add optional shared-state foundation

question: Should OpenClaw accept a core durable shared-state boundary now, and if so should this first storage slice expose configuration beyond the single approved activation path before any owner-facing runtime integration exists?
rationale: The branch changes shared persistent state and public configuration, but the linked RFC says the owner boundary and stack direction are not yet accepted; code review cannot choose that permanent product contract safely.

options.title: Sponsor a narrowed core boundary
options.body: Accept only a named residual core responsibility, then require a rebased slice with inactive worker and retention settings removed and live upgrade proof.

options.title: Keep durability owner-specific
options.body: Reject the shared residual layer and keep any cross-owner recovery evidence within existing task, flow, subagent, delivery, and session owners.

options.title: Pause the implementation series
options.body: Leave the RFC open for further owner analysis and defer persistent schema work until a maintainer sponsors a concrete user-facing need.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrowed core boundary
recommendation.body: Accept only a named residual core responsibility, then require a rebased slice with inactive worker and retention settings removed and live upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the identified author of both the proposal and implementation series, so they are best placed to incorporate a maintainer-sponsored scope decision; the actual upstream core-state decision owner is not established by the supplied history.
